text: The ruby-throated bulbul (Rubigula dispar), also known as the yellow bulbul, is a passerine bird belonging to the bulbul family.[1][2] It was previously classified within the genus Turdus and later placed in Pycnonotus, but molecular phylogenetic studies revealed that Pycnonotus was polyphyletic, leading to the reclassification of five bulbul species, including the ruby-throated bulbul, into the genus Rubigula.[2][4] Originally, it was considered conspecific with other Rubigula bulbuls, such as the flame-throated bulbul,[3] and until 2008, it was also regarded as conspecific with the black-capped, black-crested, flame-throated, and Bornean bulbuls; however, these are now recognized as distinct species.[5][2] The bird measures 17–20 cm in length, is virtually crestless, has a black head with a deep red throat, greenish-yellow back and wings, yellow underparts, and a greenish-black tail, with black bill and legs.[6] It inhabits forest and dense scrub environments. The ruby-throated bulbul constructs its nest in bushes, typically laying two to four eggs. Its diet consists of fruit and insects. This Pycnonotidae-related article is a stub.
